decision.summary: Round 3, escalated to a full review because review-diff.json reported auto_escalated true. No blocking findings. The three changed claims are sound: claim-047 and claim-048 are verbatim in seg-0091 and seg-0019 with correct speakers and fair characterisations, and claim-028's values key now names the $40 billion figure as excess capital rather than buyback capacity, which is what Dimon actually says in seg-0079. Section 7's outlier-losses sentence now cites claim-047, which does contain the statement. All six web sources cited in the brief were opened and each is what it claims to be. Temporal integrity holds: every cited source is dated on or before the 14 July 2026 event, and the two undated peer releases are same-morning Q2 results with no post-event knowledge. Deterministic gates all passed with 48 claims and zero issues, the injection scan was clean, period labelling is unambiguous and agrees with the SEC half-year facts, and the prose is bank-specific throughout. One medium finding: the evidence appendix attributes to claim-027 a sentence that is not claim-027's stored quote. It is genuine text from the same segment and speaker so the substance is unaffected, but appendix quotes are not machine-checked and a standing extractor lesson already forbids exactly this. Six low findings follow: the appendix omits entries for claim-005, claim-006 and claim-015 although all three are cited in the body; the headline sentence drops the 'excluding significant items' qualifier that claim-001 carries; the word 'organically' in section 3 is not in either cited claim; the trailing clause of section 9 attributes a forward-looking efficiency statement to management that neither cited claim contains; the brief never surfaces that headline revenue and headline expenses both grew 15% year-on-year, which is the most obvious counterpoint to its operating-leverage framing; and claim-022's 'broad-based' wording sits awkwardly against Dimon's explicit 'this is not across the board'.
